title: FLORA PRE K SCREENING
full_story:
Parents of all 3 year and 4-year-old children residing in Flora Community Unit School District are invited to bring their children to the district’s pre-k screening.  If your child is currently enrolled as a preschool student or has previously been screened you DO NOT need to have another screening.

The screenings will be held on March 18th, 19th, and 20th at the First Christian Church, located on the corner of North Main and West 4th Street.

Parents should make an appointment by going to the Flora School website to complete the Pre-K Screening Form, and you will be contacted with a screening time for your child.  If you have any questions, call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs.

Pre-K Students must have family income documentation on file in order to determine eligibility for the program.  Parents should bring income information, certified birth certificate, immunization record, lead screening result, Social Security Number, and school physical for their child to be in the Pre-K Program.

The Flora Unit # 35 P.A.T Prevention Initiative will be offering free developmental screenings for children ages birth to three during the Flora Pre-K Screenings.  Early detection of developmental delays will benefit a child for a lifetime.  If you are interested, please call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs to make an appointment.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble village board met in regular session Monday evening.

Mayor Brad Kessler reported that the Village’s water tower needs maintenance.  The proposed work includes a complete abrasive blast cleaning of both the interior and exterior of the existing potable water elevated storage tank, followed by the application of new interior and exterior coating systems with an expected lifespan of 25+ years.  The estimated cost for the project is $486,400.00.  Mike Bridges presented two possible loan options, the Rural Development Loan which would structure the financing over 40 years but would come with a higher interest rate.  Or, the TEPA Loan Program which would be structured over 20 years at an estimated interest rate of 2.16%, or possibly lower.  The anticipated annual repayment for the Village would be approximately $28,320.  Bridges noted that the application and approval process will take time.  He recommended submitting the IEPA application promptly if the Board wishes to pursue this option.  Completing the application does not obligate the Village to the project; it simply places the Village on the priority list.  This list is issued only twice per year, and it is unlikely the Village would be placed on the first available list.

Bridges also discussed the bids that were opened on February 18th, for the Cherry-Palmer Street Drainage Project.  There were two bids, one from Coner Travis for $9,720.00 and one from Enlow Inc for $4,430.00.  A motion was made to accept the bid from Enlow Inc.

Residents were reminded that the Noble Lions Club breakfast will be held on Saturday and were also asked to please remove ground decorations from the Noble Cemetery by March 31st.

title: MILES OF SMILES AT CLAY CITY
full_story:
The Clay City School District will be hosting Miles of Smiles on March 4th.  Miles of Smiles, Ltd. is providing preventative dental services at Clay City to eligible children in all grades.

Services may include an exam/screening by a licensed dentist or licensed and certified public health dental hygienist, a cleaning, fluoride varnish application, and sealant placement if needed.  This also satisfies the dental requirement mandated by the State of Illinois for school children for Kindergarten, 2nd, 6th, and 9th grades.  There is no cost to the family or the school district.  After the services are performed, the following entities will be billed where applicable: IL Medicaid Program, public/private grants, or private dental insurance.

Miles of Smiles, Ltd. will accept any reimbursement as the final payment, even if the claim is denied.  The families and the schools are never billed for any copayments, deductibles, or balances.

Consent forms can be returned to school nurse Ms. Withrow or you may register your student online by scanning the QR code on the Miles of Smiles forms.  Please contact Ms. Withrow at [email protected] if you have any questions or concerns.

title: WABASH COMMUNICATIONS SCHOLARSHIP
full_story:
Applications are now open for Wabash Communications scholarships.  Wabash Communications is awarding more than $20,000 to graduating seniors in the service area to help with college, trade school, or certification programs.

Wabash Communications awards more than $20,000 in scholarships annually to graduating high school seniors across the service area.

To qualify for the Wabash Communications scholarships your parent or legal guardian must be a member/customer of Wabash Communications or Wabash Communications Co-op, you plan to continue your education after high school at University or College, Junior college, Trade school, or Certification program.  Any field of study qualifies, there is no GPA minimum, and there are no extracurricular requirements.

Education is expensive.  These scholarships are meant to help offset those costs so students can stay focused on what’s next, whether that’s college, technical training, or a certification program.  If you’re continuing your education, you’re eligible to apply.

The application process is straightforward, complete the application and required information at https://wabash.net/scholarships/.  Submit your application by March 6th there is no application fee.

If you’re a graduating senior and meet the eligibility requirements, don’t wait.  This is an opportunity to receive financial support from a local cooperative that’s invested in your future.

title: PESTICIDE LICENSE RENEWAL
full_story:
Whether renewing an Illinois pesticide license or applying for one, registration is now open for local in-person testing sessions to be held in Olney, Fairfield, and Effingham.

While the testing is provided by the Illinois Department of Agriculture in collaboration with Illinois Extension, it is for pesticide applicators and operators who need a commercial, private, or special license, the in-person testing is free and will be available in Richland, Wayne, and Effingham Counties through March.  Registration is required and early sign up is encouraged due to class size limitations.  With all in-person testing from 10:00 to 1:00 each day.

The next testing date at the Farm Bureau Office in Effingham is on March 4th with a morning and evening session.  The next testing date in Richland County is on March 13th.  And the next testing date at the Extension Office in Fairfield will be on March 19th.

To register, visit the IDOA website at www.agr.illinois.gov/pesticides/in-person-testing or contact your Extension Office in Olney, Fairfield, or Effingham.

title: LAKE LAND CAREER CONFERENCE
full_story:
On April 9th and 10th, Lake Land College and the Education for Employment System 340 will co-host the 8th grade career conference, an annual event designed to help young students discover rewarding, local career paths.

During the event, students will meet with local employers representing a wide range of industries, including agriculture, healthcare, manufacturing, business and more.  Students will have the opportunity to ask questions, explore their interests, learn about educational requirements and draw career inspiration from accomplished professionals.

Employers are invited to host a table at the event to connect with students.  The event will be held in the Lake Land College Field House from 9:30 am to 1:30 pm both days.  Participating businesses have the option to attend either one or both conference days.  A complimentary lunch will also be provided for all company representatives.

Employers interested in attending the event must register ahead of time.

For more information about the 8th grade career conference, contact Kaurin at 217-234-5032 or [email protected].
